Eleonore does beautiful grooming, however, the owner is awful, never says hello, never a kind word, just there to take your money. Anyway, despite everything, as a former client, I continued to go to this salon because of Eleonore's work, whom I had known for a long time.

Recently, I made an appointment for grooming, but Eleonore returned my dog ​​washed but without having done the haircut. This can happen, as she had understood that she was only supposed to give him a bath, and I thought she knew it was a haircut since it was written on the appointment.
A misunderstanding can happen, and it's not a big deal in itself, even if it means I have to travel again and take half a day off work because I don't live nearby.

So, I immediately and very politely asked to come back so that the haircut could be done and to pay the extra fee. Which is only fair.

But the owner didn't call me back, and when I did, she was aggressive and rude for no reason, and wanted me to pay for the entire grooming again just two days later! She refused to acknowledge that I had booked an appointment for a haircut (which is clearly noted on their booking) and that it was completely unacceptable to charge me €85 for grooming again. When I pointed this out to her because I was shocked, especially since I was a returning customer, she wouldn't let me explain and told me she didn't want me as a client anymore. What blatant dishonesty, only greed. I'm disgusted and shocked by her behavior. Anyway, I have no regrets. Too bad for Eleonore, who is very nice.

I've been bringing my dog ​​to be groomed here for several years now, and I'm always very happy. Thank you to the whole team, and especially to Alexandra, the manager.

CATASTROPHIC EXPERIENCE – BEHAVIOR OF THE NEW MANAGER

As a customer of La Tour Câline for OVER 10 years, with the previous owner with whom everything always went very well, I am now angry and extremely disappointed by the change since the takeover.

I entrusted my Japanese Spitz to them for grooming, which cost €95. The result was absolutely not up to my expectations: an uneven cut, botched finishing touches, and even a knot that was still there. I therefore expressed my dissatisfaction and asked what could be done to rectify the situation. The appointment was agreed upon.

However, the real problem was the attitude of the new manager. Instead of handling a customer complaint professionally, she immediately became defensive, twisted the situation, and accused me of having trimmed my dog's fur myself at home, which is completely untrue.

She also asked me: "What do you want to fix?" Actually, she's the professional: as a client, I'm not supposed to explain how to fix a haircut. When I simply mentioned my concern about the undercoat of my Japanese Spitz, she shouted into the phone, "You're not going to teach me my job!"

During this exchange, I could hear my stressed dog barking in the background, which only increased my anxiety, and I ran to get my dog.

After a service costing almost €100, I find it UNACCEPTABLE to be treated this way. Mistakes and dissatisfaction can happen, but to blame a loyal client of over 10 years instead of reflecting on one's own practices... that takes some doing.

In my opinion, there's a real lack of self-reflection and a level of customer service that's no longer what I've experienced over the years.

Clarification following your response:

Your response confirms exactly what I'm criticizing: no self-reflection, only accusations aimed at discrediting a loyal customer of over 10 years.

You claim the haircut was perfect. In that case, why did you agree to redo it? A customer doesn't ask for a fix on a €95 grooming service without reason.

You even go so far as to mention my daughter in your public response. I find that particularly inappropriate.

A child has no place in a conflict between adults. As she was leaving your salon, she simply told me, "The lady was putting her hands towards you, I was angry." That's all she took away from the incident.

As for my 60-year-old mother, you had no qualms about attacking her because she used the word "disgusting" to describe the result of the haircut. At nearly €100 per service, a client has every right to express their dissatisfaction.

A "professional" is supposed to listen to a complaint, not turn criticism into a conflict.

Finally, it was only after publishing my review that I discovered other negative testimonials from former clients since the salon's reopening, including one concerning a Samoyed.

I therefore realize that I am unfortunately not an isolated case.

I stand by my opinion in its entirety. Readers will form their own opinions after reading our exchanges.
